fact: Reasoning is named as the third function of the mind
God expects you to engage your mind in reasoning, which is why He invites you in Isaiah 1:18, 'Come now, and let us reason together...'
To reason implies to engage in rational, logical and analytical thinking
To reason also means good judgment and sound sense
The end product of reasoning is quality decisions, and reasoning enhances the quality of decisions you make
After the invitation in Isaiah 1:18, verse 19 says 'If ye be willing and obedient, ye shall eat the good of the land'
The condition for eating the good of the land is being willing and obedient
It therefore means that reasoning is required if you must gain access into your inheritance on earth
Reasoning involves looking at issues objectively with a view to locating the right step to take, and processing issues in your mind to draw intelligent conclusions
Isaiah 41:21 is cited: 'Produce your cause... bring forth your strong reasons...', meaning God expects you to be a deep thinker so you can bring forth strong reasons
God's 'Come and let us reason together' is glossed as 'Don't die in that cage. That's not your destiny. Sit up mentally, let's look at it together'

The prodigal son is the worked example of reasoning, and Luke 15:17-18 is quoted: 'And when he came to himself, he said, How many hired servants of my father's have bread enough and to spare, and I perish with hunger! I will arise and go to my father...'
The prodigal son reasoned his way back to a colourful destiny, and simply engaged the art of reasoning to terminate his sufferings
The prodigal son probably asked himself: Where am I? How did I get here? Do I want to be out of here? What does it take to be out of where I am and to get to where I'm going?
Nowhere are we told that the prodigal son prayed or fasted; all he did was reason his way back to colour and beauty
The Church has long lost the art of thinking, and the enemy has taken advantage of this
God will not think or plan the food you will eat for you; no matter how hard you pray, God will not think for you, because it is your responsibility to think, not His
God counts on your reasoning
Luke 14:28 is the parable cited under 'Sit Down First': 'For which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost, whether he have sufficient to finish it?'
Every tower builder is a tower thinker
You need to first sit down and think it through, reasoning within yourself: This is where I'm going, how do I get there? What does it take to get there? How prepared am I to get there?
Everything you see on the outside begins from the inside, and everything you see in the open started in the secret
When Jesus was confronted with the woman caught in adultery He stooped down and engaged in the art of reasoning, writing on the ground as if He had not heard them while thinking the issue through
Having thought through, Jesus looked up and challenged them with John 8:7, 'He that is without sin among you, let him first cast a stone at her'
What reasoning guarantees is a rising
You need to count the cost, find out what it takes, and see how prepared you are, before making a move, which is why reasoning makes you a high-flier in the race of life
The Ministry was commissioned on a Saturday and the following Monday work started in the office, and it has remained open ever since
Before they started, everything they would need to get going was in place, and the structure they would use for the next 20 years was in place
It took 26 months of first sitting down and planning, through mental processing of objectives and laying hold of a good understanding of what the mission statement was
A man told the author that when he earned one thousand naira he had enough to spend, when he earned five thousand naira he still had excess, and even at twenty thousand naira it was still enough
The author's conclusion from that story is that what you have is enough, if only you can think well
That man was a professor who built a house without an overdraft, a neat and heaven-bound Christian not involved in any dubious business
When the author was earning three hundred naira he did not borrow, and he always had brought forward
You are not a beggar because you don't have enough, you are borrowing because you can't think enough
Most of our old parents were peasant farmers, some never even saw one hundred naira together at a time, but they still built houses
Today you find people who earn fifty thousand naira a month and yet have not been able to build anything, not even a room, a case of the more the income the greater the waste
The man who has not built arrives in the village with his whole family yelling 'Is my room ready?', all because he is not thinking
